O.outcome_detail: self-reported competence delivering mental health education

cells.quote: The item “I feel competent delivering mental health education to students” was significantly different for school staff (M = 3.27, SD = 1.09) and allied health professionals (M = 4.25, SD = .77; t (85.94) = −4.96, p < .001, g = 1.00).
cells.note: Allied health professionals reported greater competence than school staff; group assignment was not random.

O.outcome_detail: whether professional training addressed mental health education for students

cells.quote: Welch’s t-test found significant differences in “My professional training addressed mental health education for students” between school staff ( M = 1.96, SD = 1.07) and allied health professionals (M = 3.58, SD = 1.23; t (68.29) = −6.43, p < .001), and the magnitude of the difference was large (Hedge’s g = 1.42).
cells.note: Allied health professionals reported that their professional training addressed mental health education more than school staff; group assignment was not random.

O.outcome_detail: belief that school-based mental health initiatives strengthen academic performance

cells.note: Allied health professionals endorsed this belief more strongly than school staff; group assignment was not random.
